title: Radon–Nikodym derivative as a ratio of point masses
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite measurable space carrying two finite measures $\mu$ and $
u$ with $\mu \ll 
u$, and let $\omega \in \Omega$ be a point whose singleton has positive mass, $
u(\{\omega\}) 
eq 0$. Then the Radon–Nikodym derivative of $\mu$ with respect to $
u$ takes at $\omega$ the value
\[
   rac{d\mu}{d
u}(\omega) =  rac{\mu(\{\omega\})}{
u(\{\omega\})},
\]
where both sides are read as nonnegative real numbers.
hypotheses_covered: Ω is a finite (and discrete) measurable space
μ and ν are finite measures
μ is absolutely continuous with respect to ν
ω is a point of Ω
replaced:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite measurable space, $\mu \ll \nu$ finite measures, and $\omega \in \Omega$
with $\nu\{\omega\} \neq 0$.  Then the real-valued Radon--Nikodym derivative satisfies
\[
  \left(\frac{d\mu}{d\nu}(\omega)\right).\mathrm{toReal}
  = \frac{\mu.\mathrm{real}\,\{\omega\}}{\nu.\mathrm{real}\,\{\omega\}}.
\]
